While the data was largely in line with expectations, it’s worth emphasizing that if we exclude food and energy, and look at what’s known as core CPI, prices rose 0.3% last month, which was worse than expected. For the fifth month in a row, inflation has climbed faster than wages, squeezing consumers already struggling with an affordability crisis. [...] > Prices for a wide swath of goods and services continued to climb in August, according to a report Friday that raises the specter of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week.
>
> The consumer price index rose a seasonally adjusted 0.4% for the month, putting the 12-month increase at 3.4%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday
results.title: Consumer prices continued to climb in August, as inflation concerns persist

Furth said even though he’s been paying more to truck in products a lot of his customers — which make, say, fig bars using fig paste they buy from him — have been pushing back against price hikes, out of concern grocery shoppers might not buy them if they’re too expensive.

“So our customers who make the fig bars are very, very careful to try to hold their cost down, because they don’t want to lose sales,” he said.

That means Furth’s company has to eat the cost instead.
